NEWS AND VIEWS 03 June 2020 Large-scale early Maya sites in Mexico revealed by lidar mapping technology Archaeology is transforming our view of how ancient Maya societies developed.
Lidar is changing archaeological study of the ancient Maya in Mexico and Central America.
Use of lidar technology has now led to the discovery that large, monumental structures that aid naked-eye astronomy were built unexpectedly early.

A more-recent transformative innovation is the airborne application of a remote-sensing technique called light detection and ranging (lidar) to create a model (also known as a digital-elevation model) of the bare-surface terrain that is hidden by trees in forested areas1.
